question: Does the Qwen before/after CoT-control difference persist among traces of comparable observed reasoning length?

primary.eligibility: nonempty reasoning, at least 20 whitespace-delimited words, closed thinking block, nonempty final response, no length truncation
primary.algorithm: Within each stratum, maximize pair count without replacement among the three before and three after decoding samples; then minimize total absolute log length difference; never use outcome scores in matching.
primary.aggregation: paired means over matched traces; also equal-weight the eight constraint types when all have matches
primary.uncertainty: 5000 paired bootstrap replicates of matched item clusters, preserving all selected seed pairs within an item

sensitivities.eligibility: primary eligibility; additionally token-ratio 1.1 with any nonempty reasoning including incomplete traces

interpretation: Descriptive comparison restricted to observed length overlap. Length and completion are post-training outcomes; matching them does not identify a causal effect independent of length. Report coverage, excluded traces, per-constraint differences and length balance. No new generations or compute rental.

exploratory_addition_after_first_matchin.comparison: Also require both word and token lengths to differ by no more than 10%, using the larger log-ratio as matching cost.
exploratory_addition_after_first_matchin.reason: Token-only matches can differ substantially in word count because case changes and meow insertion change tokenization.
exploratory_addition_after_first_matchin.inference: Report strict improved/regressed pairs and item-cluster sign-flip P values alongside bootstrap intervals; few discordant items can make percentile intervals misleading.
exploratory_addition_after_first_matchin.bootstrap_rng: Seed each configuration using SHA256(config) XOR 20261030, so adding a sensitivity does not change other configurations.
